newsitem.title: UK: UK industry leaders criticise budget tax changes.
newsitem.headline: UK industry leaders criticise budget tax changes.

text.p: Britain's Institute of Directors on Wednesday criticised the Labour government's windfall tax on utilities and abolition of tax credits paid to pension funds introduced in its first budget since it came to power in May.
Director General Tim Melville-Ross said in a statement the Institute welcomed cuts in corporation tax rates for big and small firms, which would give incentives to start up or expand businesses.
But he said, "We are very disappointed about the windfall tax and the abolition of tax credits."

The IOD said removing tax credits on dividends would hit pension funds hard and would increase burdens for both employers and employees. It would also reduce the attractiveness of saving for retirement.
Ross also said the IoD was concerned about the government's decision to spend 44 percent of next year's reserve so early on. "This will leave little margin to cope with any spending overshoots."
